content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To make olive oil and rosemary grissini, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Infuse olive oil with a sprig of rosemary over low heat (10 minutes)
Step 2. Sift the bread flour into a large mixing bowl (2 minutes)
Step 3. Bloom the active dry yeast in warm water (10 minutes)
Step 4. Measure out the sea salt (1 minute)
Step 5. Finely chop fresh rosemary leaves (5 minutes)
Step 6. Warm the honey slightly to make it pourable (30 seconds)
Step 7. Mix the infused oil into the warm water (2 minutes)
Step 8. Weigh the whole wheat flour (2 minutes)
Step 9. Grate fresh parmesan cheese (5 minutes)
Step 10. Calibrate the kitchen scale (1 minute)
Step 11. Combine the yeast mixture with the flour blend (3 minutes)
Step 12. Line the baking sheets with parchment paper (2 minutes)
Step 13. Measure the total water volume required (1 minute)
Step 14. Dust the work surface with flour (1 minute)
Step 15. Prepare a small bowl of water for sealing dough (1 minute)
Step 16. Lightly oil a proofing bowl (1 minute)
Step 17. Begin the initial dough mixing by hand (5 minutes)
Step 18. Set the oven to the proofing setting (2 minutes)
Step 19. Whisk the wet ingredients together (1 minute)
Step 20. Fold the chopped rosemary into the dough (4 minutes)
Step 21. Prepare the rolling pin (1 minute)
Step 22. Add the remaining flour to adjust consistency (5 minutes)
Step 23. Knead the dough until smooth and elastic (10 minutes)
Step 24. Clean the mixing tools (5 minutes)
Step 25. Combine the dry flours in a secondary container (2 minutes)
Step 26. Transfer dough to the oiled proofing bowl (1 minute)
Step 27. Check the room temperature for fermentation (1 minute)
Step 28. Organize the workstation for shaping (5 minutes)
Step 29. Sharpen the dough scraper (3 minutes)
Step 30. Cover the bowl with a damp cloth (1 minute)
Step 31. Gradually incorporate salt into the dough (3 minutes)
Step 32. Allow the dough to rest for the first rise (1 hour)
Step 33. Prepare a glaze of olive oil and salt (3 minutes)
Step 34. Sanitize the countertop (10 minutes)
Step 35. Punch down the risen dough (1 minute)
Step 36. Divide the dough into equal portions (8 minutes)
Step 37. Scale the dough portions to 20 grams each (10 minutes)
Step 38. Clear a space for the finished grissini to cool (5 minutes)
Step 39. Select the best quality extra virgin olive oil (2 minutes)
Step 40. Sift a small amount of decorative flour (1 minute)
Step 41. Shape each portion into a small ball (10 minutes)
Step 42. Measure the length of the baking sheet (1 minute)
Step 43. Wash the rosemary sprigs (2 minutes)
Step 44. Place the dough in a warm, draft-free spot (2 minutes)
Step 45. Dry the chopped rosemary thoroughly (5 minutes)
Step 46. Set out the cooling racks (2 minutes)
Step 47. Retrieve the rolling board (1 minute)
Step 48. Roll each ball into a long, thin rope (15 minutes)
Step 49. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit (15 minutes)
Step 50. Activate the kitchen timer (10 seconds)
Step 51. Dissolve honey into the warm water (1 minute)
Step 52. Place the grissini ropes onto the baking sheets (5 minutes)
Step 53. Mix a topping of salt and pepper (2 minutes)
Step 54. Brush the dough ropes with the oil glaze (5 minutes)
Step 55. Let the shaped grissini rest for a second rise (20 minutes)
Step 56. Verify the yeast expiration date (30 seconds)
Step 57. Prepare the storage airtight container (2 minutes)
Step 58. Sprinkle the parmesan and rosemary over the ropes (4 minutes)
Step 59. Measure the black pepper (1 minute)
Step 60. Check the oven thermometer (1 minute)
Step 61. Grind the sea salt (2 minutes)
Step 62. Bake the grissini until golden brown (15 minutes)
Step 63. Rotate the baking sheets halfway through (1 minute)
Step 64. Dampen the kitchen towel (30 seconds)
Step 65. Fill a spray bottle with water for steam (2 minutes)
Step 66. Mist the oven interior to create steam (30 seconds)
Step 67. Fetch the olive oil from the pantry (1 minute)
Step 68. Remove grissini from the oven (1 minute)
Step 69. Inspect the rosemary for freshness (1 minute)
Step 70. Locate the baking sheets (2 minutes)
